prompt: Explain the concept of encapsulation in object-oriented programming. NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT 1: Do not use the words 'data', 'hide', or 'class'. NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT 2: Format the output as a Markdown table with two columns: 'Concept' and 'Description'.
response_text:
| Concept                     | Description                                                                                                                                                                 |
|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Bundling of state & behavior| Encapsulation groups an object’s internal state together with the functions that operate on that state, keeping them as a single, coherent unit.                           |
| Access control mechanisms   | By exposing only selected operations (often called methods) and keeping the rest inaccessible, the object protects its inner workings from unintended external interference. |
| Public interface            | The visible operations form a contract that other parts of the program can rely on, allowing interaction without needing to know the underlying implementation details.       |
| Benefits (maintainability, modularity) | Because the inner workings can be altered without affecting code that uses the object, systems become easier to evolve, test, and reuse.                                 |
